# Issue #47: flag parsing treats "off " as true

A setting written as `off ` with a trailing space ends up enabled. This showed up
when reading feature switches from the environment. Please fix the flag parsing.


Repository files:
flags/__init__.py
flags/parse.py
tests/test_parse.py

1| """Parsing of on/off switches from configuration text."""
   2| 
   3| _FALSE_WORDS = frozenset({"0", "false", "no", "off"})
   4| 
   5| 
   6| def parse_flag(text):
   7|     """Interpret one switch word as a bool.
   8| 
   9|     Matching is case-insensitive and ignores whitespace around the word.
  10|     "0", "false", "no" and "off" are False; any other non-empty word is True.
  11|     Raises ValueError if the text is empty or only whitespace.
  12|     """
  13|     word = text.lower()
  14|     if not word:
  15|         raise ValueError("empty flag")
  16|     return word not in _FALSE_WORDS
  17| 
  18| 
  19| def parse_flags(text):
  20|     """Parse a comma-separated list of switch words into a list of bools.
  21| 
  22|     Each item is interpreted with `parse_flag`. Items that are empty or only
  23|     whitespace are skipped, so "" gives [] and "on,,off" gives [True, False].
  24|     """
  25|     return [parse_flag(part) for part in text.split(",") if part.strip()]

1| import unittest
   2| from flags import parse_flag, parse_flags
   3| 
   4| 
   5| class TestFlags(unittest.TestCase):
   6|     def test_words(self):
   7|         self.assertTrue(parse_flag("on"))
   8|         self.assertTrue(parse_flag("YES"))
   9|         self.assertFalse(parse_flag("off"))
  10|         self.assertFalse(parse_flag("False"))
  11| 
  12|     def test_list(self):
  13|         self.assertEqual(parse_flags("on,off,yes"), [True, False, True])
  14| 
  15|     def test_list_with_spaces(self):
  16|         self.assertEqual(parse_flags("on, off ,yes"), [True, False, True])
  17|

The bug is clear: `parse_flag` lowercases but never strips whitespace, so `"off "` doesn't match the false-words set (and the docstring promises whitespace is ignored). The fix is to strip before comparing:
Now the `if not word` check also correctly handles whitespace-only input, matching the docstring. Let me verify:
Tests pass. Quick sanity check on the exact case from the issue:

arguments.command:
python -c "
from flags import parse_flag, parse_flags
print(parse_flag('off '))       # False (was True)
print(parse_flag(' off'))       # False
print(parse_flag('ON'))         # True
print(parse_flags('on, off ,yes'))
print(parse_flags('on,,off'))
try:
    parse_flag('   ')
except ValueError as e:
    print('ValueError:', e)
"

All fixed. The issue was in `parse_flag` in `flags/parse.py`: it lowercased the input but didn't strip whitespace, so `"off "` wasn't recognized as a false word and fell through to the "any other word is True" branch. Adding `.strip()` before `.lower()` makes the behavior match the documented contract (case-insensitive, whitespace-ignoring), and also makes whitespace-only input correctly raise `ValueError`.

arguments.summary: Fixed flag parsing in flags/parse.py by stripping whitespace before lowercasing in parse_flag (`word = text.strip().lower()`). Previously "off " (with trailing space) didn't match the false-words set and was treated as True; now it correctly parses as False, matching the documented behavior. Whitespace-only input now also correctly raises ValueError. All existing tests pass.
